previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Ms. ___ was admitted for worsening wheezing, cough, and shortness of breath after a prolonged course at rehab, where she had been treated for suspected pneumonia without improvement. Evaluation revealed an acute exacerbation of COPD and acute on chronic systolic heart failure, supported by elevated BNP and clinical signs of fluid overload. She was treated with a short course of high-dose prednisone, nebulized albuterol and ipratropium, and a brief increase in lasix dose, which was stopped when renal function and sodium began to decline. A CT scan of the neck and chest showed no evidence of tracheal cancer recurrence but noted new left upper lobe consolidation, which was deemed non-infectious given her clinical improvement. She remained in normal sinus rhythm on amiodarone and metoprolol. Discharge planning included a structured steroid taper, resumption of lasix only if weight exceeded 87kg, and follow-up with pulmonology, oncology in six months, and vascular surgery for planned toe amputations due to gangrene. She was discharged to extended care in stable condition.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Shortness of breath, hypoxia.

FINDINGS:  A single portable semi-erect chest radiograph was obtained.

COMPARISON:  CT ___.  

Radiographs ___ through ___.

FINDINGS:  Right lower lobe and retrocardiac opacities have significantly
worsened since ___ and now obscure the bilateral diaphragmatic
contours.  Post-surgical volume loss and minor fissure thickening are more
pronounced.  Cardiomegaly is similar.  A right shoulder prosthesis is similar.

IMPRESSION:  Significant worsening of multifocal opacities representing some
combination of atelectasis, pulmonary edema and consolidation.

INDICATION:  ___ woman with flash pulmonary edema and poor intravenous
access.  Please advance midline to central location.

PHYSICIANS:  Dr. ___ (resident) and Dr. ___ (fellow)
performed the procedure.  Dr. ___ (attending) was present for and
supervised the critical steps of the procedure.

PROCEDURE IN DETAIL:  The procedure was explained to the patient.  A
preprocedure timeout was performed.  The entry site containing the existing
PICC was prepped and draped in the usual sterile fashion.  Under fluoroscopy,
the position of the existing catheter was confirmed to be in the left axillary
vein. The skin and subcutaneous tissues were anesthetized with 2% lidocaine at
the entry site.  A guidewire was advanced through the existing catheter with
the tip in the left axillary vein.  The guidewire could not be advanced past
the axillary vein, likely due to stenosis in the subclavian vein.  The patient
confirmed that she has had a prior Port-A-Cath on the left as seen on prior
chest radiographs. After phone discussion with the ordering physician, it was
confirmed that a midline would be adequate.  The existing catheter was removed
and a peel-away sheath was placed over the guidewire.  A double-lumen Power
PICC measuring 22 cm in length was placed through the peel-away sheath with
its tip positioned in the axillary vein under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position
of the catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.  The
peel-away sheath and guidewire were removed.  The catheter was secured to the
skin, flushed and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate post-procedure
complications.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Uncomplicated fluoroscopically guided double-lumen midline placement via
the left brachial approach (per documentation of prior catheter placement). 
Final internal length is 22 cm with the tip positioned in the left axillary
vein.  The line is ready to use.
2.  Probable left subclavian vein stenosis due to prior left Port-A-Cath.

PICC line ends in axillary region.

CONCLUSION:
